https://www.thetimes.com/uk/scotland/art.title: Scotland police left in the dark over Trump’s visit
https://www.thetimes.com/uk/scotland/art.subtitle: The US president will be touring his golf courses during a five-day trip that is expected to be ‘as big as the Queen’s funeral’
https://www.thetimes.com/uk/scotland/art.text:
The White House has still not given Police Scotland sight of President Trump’s itinerary three days before a visit that will be “as big as the Queen’s funeral”, a senior officer has said.
Trump arrives in Scotland on Friday for a five-day visit, during which he will tour his golf courses in Ayrshire and Aberdeenshire, and meet Sir Keir Starmer and the first minister, John Swinney.
The scale of the operation has already prompted concern from the Scottish Police Federation over additional pressures on officers.
The president of the Association of Scottish Police Superintendents (Asps) said the visit will “undoubtedly stretch” police resources.
There will be 248 deployments around Aberdeenshire, the south and the west of the country to deal with potential protests.

However, Scotland’s police force is unable to pinpoint specifics of what will be a vast operation because it does not yet know the president’s movements.
Trump will remain in Scotland until Tuesday, making this trip longer than any previous visit.
Bond added that the force was “waiting to see how protests will manifest” but is “working on the basis” that protesters will congregate in Edinburgh, Glasgow, Aberdeenshire and Ayrshire.
Previous visits have drawn widespread demonstrations in Scotland’s main cities. In 2018 a paraglider was able to enter the no-fly zone above Trump’s golf course and fly a banner reading: “Trump: Well Below Par.”
One of the groups most vocal in its plans to protest against the US president’s visit is the Stop Trump Coalition.
Emma Bond, assistant chief constable, said “multiple venues” are being factored into the force’s planning. Beyond that, it is in the dark about the detail.
While she would not be drawn on whether the last-minute scheduling was hampering operational planning, Bond said: “The specifics of the schedule will be something for the White House to manage, and we will deal with whatever comes up. Policing continuously works in a world of ambiguity on occasion.”
Rob Hay, president of Asps, said the trip will require a “significant operation across the country over many days” from Police Scotland.
However, Swinney has insisted policing will not be put in a “detrimental position” as a result of the visit.
Bond said that, as part of its proactive policing strategy, Police Scotland will contact protest groups before planned events. However, the force has not yet contacted any groups before the US president’s tour, although there are “a number” that are expected to protest.
She said: “Let me be very clear that abusive, threatening behaviour, any activity that in any way seeks to disrupt an event or any activity that actually puts the safety of the public at risk is not lawful protest, and there may well be consequences from a criminal justice perspective.”
Police Scotland is not expecting violent protest. “I have nothing at this stage to give me any specific concern,” Bond added.
All of the force’s 84 protest liaison officers will be deployed across the weekend but Bond declined to comment on how many officers in total would be involved in the operation, nor the expected cost. Officers will be working longer shifts than usual and leave over the period has been cancelled, meaning a significant investment in overtime costs will be needed.
An appeal has been made to the Police Service of Northern Ireland for additional resources over the visit and Bond said her officers have had “direct engagement” with the US Secret Service.
Trump’s course in Aberdeenshire is to hold a tournament the day after he leaves Scotland and the force is also policing that event.
Bond said: “This is a significant and complex operation, it will have an impact on a number of parts of Scotland and the priority is to make sure that it passes off with the least amount of disruption. The focus is making sure that the president is safe while he’s here and can enjoy his time in Scotland.”
